common_name: California Dreaming Hellebore (Honeymoon Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in fall or early spring into humus-rich, well-drained shade soil; established clumps resent being moved.

directions: California Dreaming is a Honeymoon-series selection from Walters Gardens hybridizer Hans Hansen, carrying unspotted single flowers in clear yellow-gold tones about 3 inches across. Bloom runs from early into mid-spring above a mound of leathery, evergreen, deeply lobed foliage. Like its series-mates it was bred for vigorous, uniform clumps and heavy flower counts per plant compared to older open-pollinated hybridus seed strains. It tolerates root competition from nearby trees once established and resists deer and rabbit browsing.

common_name: Irish Luck Hellebore (Honeymoon Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Set out divisions in fall or early spring in part shade with rich, well-drained soil; avoid disturbing established roots.

directions: Irish Luck bears single green-toned flowers marked with a central burgundy flare at the base of each petal, opening from late winter into mid-spring above leathery evergreen foliage. As a Honeymoon-series hellebore bred by Hans Hansen for Walters Gardens, it forms a vigorous, well-branched clump with a heavier flower count than typical seed-grown Lenten roses. It is largely untroubled by deer and rabbits and, once rooted in, tolerates the dry shade found beneath established trees.

common_name: New York Night Hellebore (Honeymoon Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring into shaded beds amended with compost; established plants are long-lived and best left undisturbed.

directions: New York Night is among the darkest Honeymoon-series hellebores, with 2.5-3 inch single flowers ranging through deep grey-purple to near jet-black, held over a mound of leathery evergreen leaves. It flowers from late winter into mid-spring, giving dramatic, moody color at a time when little else blooms in the shade garden. Bred by Hans Hansen for Walters Gardens, it shares the series' trait of vigorous, uniform clumps with abundant blooms per plant. Pair it with pale or variegated companions to show off the dark petals, and remove tattered old foliage in late winter to best display the flowers.

common_name: Paris in Pink Hellebore (Honeymoon Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Install divisions in fall or early spring into humus-rich, well-drained shade soil; avoid wet, poorly drained sites that can rot the crown.

directions: Paris in Pink produces large single flowers, 3.5 to 4 inches across, in a soft light-to-medium pink, nodding above leathery, evergreen, deeply divided foliage. Bloom runs from late winter through mid-spring, and the oversized flowers make this one of the showier Honeymoon-series selections bred by Hans Hansen for Walters Gardens. It forms a dense, floriferous clump compared to older open-pollinated hybridus strains, and is deer- and rabbit-resistant. Site it where winter sun can reach the nodding blooms, or tilt the flowers upward on a slope planting to appreciate their color.

common_name: Romantic Getaway Hellebore (Honeymoon Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in fall or early spring into humus-rich, well-drained shade soil; established clumps resent being moved.

directions: Romantic Getaway carries 3-inch single white flowers centered on a dramatic red patterned eye, blooming from late winter into mid-spring over a mound of leathery evergreen foliage. The strong contrast between the white petals and bold red center markings sets it apart from softer bicolor hellebores in the Honeymoon series bred by Hans Hansen for Walters Gardens. It forms a vigorous, well-branched clump with heavy bud counts and is largely ignored by deer and rabbits. Remove old, weathered leaves in late winter just before bloom to showcase the flowers.

common_name: Rome in Red Hellebore (Honeymoon Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Set out divisions in fall or early spring in part shade with rich, well-drained soil; avoid disturbing roots once the clump is settled.

directions: Rome in Red bears single flowers, 3 to 4 inches across, in a rich maroon to wine-red that holds its saturated color well as the bloom ages. Flowering begins in late winter and continues into mid-spring over leathery, evergreen, deeply lobed foliage. As a Honeymoon-series hellebore from Hans Hansen's breeding program at Walters Gardens, it produces a notably heavy flower count per plant compared to seed-grown hybridus strains. It is deer- and rabbit-resistant and, once established, tolerates the dry shade found under deciduous trees.

common_name: Sandy Shores Hellebore (Honeymoon Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Install divisions in fall or early spring into shaded beds amended with compost; established plants are long-lived and best left undisturbed.

directions: Sandy Shores produces single flowers, 2.5 to 3 inches across, in a pale sandy apricot that deepens to a rosy pink on the petal backs, giving the nodding blooms a soft two-tone effect. It flowers from late winter into mid-spring above a clump of leathery evergreen leaves. Bred by Hans Hansen for Walters Gardens, this Honeymoon-series selection shares the series' trait of vigorous, floriferous clumps that outperform older open-pollinated hybridus seed strains. Tilt the nodding flowers upward or plant on a gentle slope to better display the warm, muted coloring.

common_name: Swiss Alps Hellebore (Honeymoon Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in fall or early spring into humus-rich, well-drained shade soil; established clumps resent being moved.

directions: Swiss Alps carries crisp white single flowers set off by a deep burgundy central eye, opening from late winter through mid-spring over a mound of leathery, evergreen, deeply divided leaves. The crisp white-and-burgundy contrast makes it one of the more striking bicolor selections in the Honeymoon series bred by Hans Hansen for Walters Gardens. Like its series-mates it forms a vigorous, heavily-flowered clump and resists deer and rabbit browsing. Cut back old, tattered foliage in late winter just before bloom to best showcase the flowers.

common_name: Tropical Sunset Hellebore (Honeymoon Series Lenten Rose)

planting.note: Set out divisions in fall or early spring in part shade with rich, well-drained soil; avoid disturbing roots once the clump is settled.

directions: Tropical Sunset bears 3-inch single flowers in creamy yellow accented with burgundy-red veining and a fine picotee edge, blooming from late winter into mid-spring above leathery evergreen foliage. The warm, sunset-toned coloring distinguishes it from the cooler pinks and whites found elsewhere in the Honeymoon series bred by Hans Hansen for Walters Gardens. It forms a dense, well-branched clump bred for heavy bloom counts compared to older seed-grown hybridus strains, and is largely unbothered by deer and rabbits. Remove weathered foliage in late winter to best display the emerging flower stems.

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Apricot Blush is part of the Winter Jewels breeding series, with large single flowers in apricot-russet tones blooming from midwinter into mid-spring.

directions: Apricot Blush is a Winter Jewels hellebore bred by Ernie and Marietta O'Byrne of Northwest Garden Nursery, producing large single flowers in blushed apricot, russet, and almost orange tones over leathery, evergreen, deeply divided foliage. Bloom begins as early as January in mild climates and continues into April, making it one of the earliest color sources in the shade garden. Like other seed-strain Winter Jewels hellebores, individual plants vary somewhat in exact shading, giving a garden-worthy range within the named color group. Remove old, tattered leaves in late winter just before flowering to best display the blooms.

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Harlequin Gem is part of the Winter Jewels breeding series, with bicolor double flowers blooming in late winter to early spring.

directions: Harlequin Gem is a double-flowered Winter Jewels selection bred by Ernie and Marietta O'Byrne, with a lighter inner collar of white, cream, yellow, or apricot sharply contrasted against outer petals streaked and edged in black-purple, crimson-purple, or maroon. Held above leathery, evergreen, deeply divided foliage, the richly patterned blooms open in late winter and persist into mid-spring. As with other Winter Jewels seed strains, individual seedlings vary somewhat in pattern and intensity within the named color theme, adding garden interest to a mass planting. Site away from areas grazed by pets or children, since all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Black Diamond is part of the Winter Jewels breeding series, with the darkest slate-purple to near-black single flowers in the strain, blooming in late winter to early spring.

directions: Black Diamond is among the darkest-flowered strains in the Winter Jewels breeding program from Ernie and Marietta O'Byrne, ranging from deep slate-purple to near-black single blooms with chartreuse nectaries, often paired with purple-tinged young foliage. Flowering runs from late winter into mid-spring over a clump of leathery, evergreen, deeply lobed leaves. The near-black coloring reads almost solid in low winter light but reveals subtle plum and charcoal undertones up close, making it a dramatic foil for paler companions. Remove old foliage in late winter just ahead of bloom to best showcase the flowers.

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Picotee Pearl is part of the Winter Jewels breeding series, with pearly white double flowers edged in red-violet, blooming in late winter to early spring.

directions: Picotee Pearl is a double-flowered Winter Jewels selection from Ernie and Marietta O'Byrne, with bright white outer petals finely edged in a thin red-violet picotee line and an inner collar of petaloid stamens patterned in the same color. The pearly, finely outlined blooms open in late winter and continue into mid-spring above leathery, evergreen, deeply divided foliage. Like other Winter Jewels seed strains, the exact depth of the picotee edge varies slightly from plant to plant within the named color group. Keep soil evenly moist while plants establish, and remove tattered old leaves in late winter to best display the flowers.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring in part shade to shade with fertile, well-drained soil; Glenda's Gloss is grown as much for its silver-veined evergreen foliage as for its flowers.

directions: Glenda's Gloss is a Frostkiss-series hellebore (patented as Helleborus x iburgensis 'Glenda's Gloss', US PP 28,008) bred by Rodney Davey and Lynda Windsor of RD Plants in the UK, combining the marbled, silver-veined evergreen foliage typical of H. x ericsmithii parentage with abundant, outward-facing white flowers blushed pink on the reverse of each petal. Bloom begins as early as mid-February and continues into spring, held on upright spikes above the patterned leaves. The silvery foliage remains attractive year-round, making this selection a dual-purpose foliage-and-flower plant for the shaded border. It is deer-resistant and performs best with consistent moisture in humus-rich soil.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring in part shade with fertile, well-drained soil; Cheryl's Shine is a compact, sterile Frostkiss hybrid grown for both foliage and flower.

directions: Cheryl's Shine (patented as Helleborus x iburgensis 'Cheryl's Shine', US PP 28,009) is a sterile Frostkiss-series hybrid of H. x ballardiae and H. x hybridus bred by Rodney Davey and Lynda Windsor of RD Plants in the UK, bearing outward-facing pink flowers that lighten toward the center around a prominent cluster of yellow stamens. Blooming begins as early as mid-February and continues into spring over green, silver-veined, evergreen foliage. Its compact habit and marbled leaves give it year-round presence in the shaded border even once flowering ends. It is deer-resistant and, being sterile, does not self-seed the way open-pollinated Lenten roses can.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring in part shade with fertile, well-drained soil; Moondance combines marbled evergreen foliage with early, outward-facing flowers.

directions: Moondance (patented as Helleborus x iburgensis 'Moondance', US PP 27,969) is a Frostkiss-series hybrid bred by Rodney Davey and Lynda Windsor of RD Plants in the UK that pairs black-green, silver-veined evergreen leaves with outfacing white flowers carrying a subtle chartreuse blush at the center. Flower spikes reach about 18 inches and open as early as mid-February, continuing into spring. Combining three hellebore species in its parentage, it is a sterile selection grown for its reliable, heavy bloom and its ornamental foliage, which stays attractive well after flowering ends. It prefers part sun to light shade and benefits from consistently moist, humus-rich soil.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring in part shade to shade with fertile, well-drained soil; Illumi Lime pairs marbled foliage with chartreuse flowers for winter and spring interest.

directions: Illumi Lime is a Frostkiss-series hellebore bred by Rodney Davey and Lynda Windsor of RD Plants in the UK, distinguished by an abundance of lime-green flowers held above marbled, silver-veined evergreen foliage, blooming through winter into spring. The chartreuse coloring is unusual among hellebores and pairs well with the mottled leaf pattern shared by other Frostkiss selections bred from H. x ericsmithii and H. x ballardiae lines. It forms a tidy, mounding clump suited to part sun through shade in well-drained, humus-rich soil. As with its series-mates, the patterned foliage remains ornamental through the growing season after flowering finishes.

common_name: Visions in White Delight Astilbe (Improved White Chinensis Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Visions in White Delight is an improved, sturdier-stemmed selection within the Visions series.

directions: Visions in White Delight is a compact Astilbe chinensis selection in the Visions series, bearing pure white, densely packed plumes on thick, strong stems above coarse, deep green foliage from midsummer into late summer. It was selected as an improvement on the original patented 'Vision in White,' with a more upright habit and sturdier flower stalks that resist flopping after rain. Like other chinensis selections it tolerates brief dry spells better than many arendsii hybrids, though it still flowers best with steady moisture in humus-rich soil. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain dense, well-colored plumes.
